‘Most bearish thing for XMR’ — What KuCoin’s Monero delisting means for liquidity

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that kuCoin is in the news today after announcing that it would remove Monero [XMR] spot trading on 30th November.
  • With such a large trading venue leaving, where would Monero traders go next?
  • Industry observers note that kuCoin has scheduled the removal of XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC for 08:00 UTC on 30th November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that kuCoin is in the news today after announcing that it would remove Monero [XMR] spot trading on 30th November. The exchange’s XMR/USDT and XMR/USDC pairs accounted for over half of Monero’s spot trading volume on CoinGecko.

With such a large trading venue leaving, where would Monero traders go next?

Industry observers note that kuCoin has scheduled the removal of XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC for 08:00 UTC on 30th November. Deposits have already been closed permanently too.

Withdrawals will close at 08:00 UTC on 31st December 2026. KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier over project-related complications, with the exchange also warning that stablecoin conversion of remaining balances won’t be guaranteed.

At press time, CoinGecko highlighted $90.42 million in combined 24-hour volumes across KuCoin’s XMR/USDT and XMR/USDC pairs. Together, they accounted for 50.27% of Monero’s spot trading volume.

Including XMR/BTC and XMR/ETH, that brought KuCoin’s total to $104.60 million or 58.14%.

Hence, the question: Where could that trading move now? At the time of writing, the remaining exchanges demonstrated more buy orders close to the market price, despite reporting a lower turnover.

Kraken’s XMR/USD pair had approximately $386,970 in buy orders within 2% below its price, compared to KuCoin’s XMR/USDT pair’s $85,683. WhiteBIT and HTX’s XMR/USDT pairs showed $260,810 and $196,231, respectively.

That gave Kraken roughly 4.5 times KuCoin’s nearby buying depth, with WhiteBIT and HTX also offering larger buy-side cushions. These orders could help absorb selling, although traders could cancel them at any time.

That access problem extended into services marketed as alternatives to CEXs.

X user and the founder of XMRHub called KuCoin’s delisting “the most bearish thing for $XMR.” According to the exec, the exchange supported swap services, liquidity, and onboarding.

It has been revealed that another X user, PerpetualCow, described the alleged connection more directly. He remarked,.

Instant swap exchanges don’t have their own liquidity, they simply wrapped around Kucoin and sold/bought into their order books.

According to recent reports, still, the proposed dependency might explain why another exchange closure could affect apparently separate services. Swap interface routing orders through KuCoin would need another supplier, sufficient inventory, or a different execution route.

Dash’s Joel Valenzuela also raised a similar concern. He warned that further CEX losses could make no-KYC Monero swaps harder to obtain.

Finally, Cake Wallet founder Vik Sharma also directed consumers towards wallet-based swaps, writing,.

Why does Monero keep getting delisted? Because it works!

It has been revealed that the announcement followed another loss of exchange access earlier that month. MEXC ended XMR spot trading on 17th November. Its XMR Perpetual Futures closed separately on 13th November.

According to recent reports, kraken, for its part, had been explicit about its own rationale. It cited regulatory changes when halting XMR trading and deposits for European Economic Area customers on 31st October 2024.

Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold has reached its highest level on record, according to Galaxy Research data. The measure peaked at 0.56 on Oct. 22 and broke the previous record of 0.50, which Galaxy dated to Nov. 6, 2020.

Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy Digital, posted about the record on X on Friday. "Bitcoin isn't digital gold? Bitcoin reaches highest correlation to gold of all time," he wrote.

Thorn shared two Galaxy Research charts together with the post. According to the charts, the 90-day correlation was at 0.54 on Nov. 23, and the 30-day correlation stood at 0.59 on the same day.

In the first half of 2026, the 90-day correlation stayed near 0.1. It started to rise in July and climbed above 0.50 by early October, according to Galaxy's data. Between 2020 and 2025, the average reading was 0.11.

On Jan. 20, Galaxy CEO Mike Novogratz wrote on X that "the gold price is telling us we are losing reserve currency status at an accelerating rate." "$BTC is disappointing as it is still being met with selling," he added.

Industry observers note that thorn wrote about Bitcoin and gold on X in February. "Bitcoin's failure to trade like gold as part of 'the debasement trade' since Sep. '25 damaged its narrative with fresh entrants," he wrote. "When bitcoiners remarked 'digital gold,' they were describing its fundamental properties, not that it's high beta to gold today," he added.

In a recent development, on Wednesday, Galaxy published a report that withdrew its Oct. 26 call on the Bitcoin bear market. "We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June," the report noted. Thorn shared it on X with the comment, "As it turns out, the Bitcoin bear market is definitely not over.".

According to the report, Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 22 at $61,104 after seven straight weekly losses. Thorn wrote in the report that the level to watch was $58,525, Bitcoin's closing low from June 30. According to Thorn, a daily close below that level would mark "the start of a move to a materially lower low.".

According to recent reports, "The clock says this bear is overdue to end; the depth says it has further to fall," the report remarked. On Nov. 22, the bear market was 412 days old, and earlier ones lasted 163 to 406 days from high to low, according to Galaxy.

Bitcoin was down 53% from its October 2025 record at that point. In past bear markets, it lost 77% to 93%. If the June low breaks, Galaxy sees possible new lows at about $48,500 and $28,200.

Galaxy tracks 13 bottom signals, and two of them have been met so far. According to the report, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs held about 1.24 million BTC, down 71,339 BTC since Oct. 4.

On Nov. 17, SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci asked Novogratz at the Digital Assets Forum in Fresh York whether Bitcoin could return to $90,000 by the end of 2026. "Unlikely now," Novogratz said. "Less likely than it was. You need something to happen," he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As no-drip, low-noise job sites become more the global rule rather than the exception, Volvo’s incredibly versatile EWR150 Electric wheeled excavators are proving to be a smart addition to construction and municipal fleets – that’s proving true in Luxembourg, as well.

According to recent reports, the Volvo EWR150 Electric wheeled excavator is helping the postage stamp nation of Luxembourg connect natural freshwater springs to a planned water reservoir, but the work has to be done in an existing groundwater protection zone, where even the smallest fuel spills or oil leaks could have serious consequences. An ideal opportunity, in other words, for a battery electric machine like the EWR150 Electric to shine.

Recent findings suggest that “Sometimes I miss the sound of the engine,” claims Thomas Weber, an operator on the project who’d previously worked with the conventional EWR150 wheeled excavator. “But the quieter operation of the EWR150 Electric is more beneficial for me, personally. Compared to the diesel equivalent, I find the performance and power to be identical.”.

Volvo CE took to LinkedIn to share the work being done by the Luxemburgers at construction firm Elenz, touting the Volvo’s clean, quiet running in this highly environment.

In a recent development, for their part, Elenz executives are equally excited about the new machine. “Going electric is not a regulation, but a requirement for this particular job,” explains Christoph Schommer, Managing Director of Elenz. “We are thoroughly impressed by the EWR150 Electric. Its low noise level is a major advantage here. At the same time, the machine offers plenty of power and consistently delivers the same level of energy.”.

In a recent development, the EWR150 Electric is built around a 270 kWh, 600V li-ion battery pack powering an electric drive motor that’s backed by a KERS-style hydraulic boom energy-recovery system that works like regenerative braking to extend the machine’s operating time. A 0.67 m³ (~0.9 yd³) bucket with 108.5-kN (~ 24,390 lb.) breakout force is standard, and offers a, 8.95 meter (~29 foot) maximum digging reach and 5.23 meter (~17 foot) digging depth. Volvo notes the machine can typically operate for 8–10 hours depending on the application.

Elenz is charging their EWR150 Electric overnight using a 32A L2 connection at a nearby sewage treatment plant, which also serves as the project office and a secure parking location for site equipment. By charging overnight, when Elenz’ crew isn’t working, the tech giant has been able to integrate the significant BEV without changing their existing work schedules.

Each Originals round combines a server seed, a client seed that the player controls, and a nonce.

Recent findings suggest that once the server seed is revealed, the player can reproduce the result with the Seeds and Verify controls built into the games. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that A different part of the bill follows an earlier timetable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Australia’s Parliament passed the Digital Duty of Care bill on Nov. 25, giving people a future route to sue covered AI chatbot providers over loss or damage caused by a breach of the fresh online safety duty. Both the duty and the right to sue are due to take effect 12 months after Royal Assent.

According to recent reports, the Nov. 25 vote completed the bill’s passage through Parliament. Schedule 2 of Australia’s Digital Duty of Care bill sets out the safety duty and the private right of action. The Senate committee’s report sets out the transition period for that schedule. The communications department confirmed on Nov. 27 that the duty would start 12 months after Royal Assent.

Recent findings suggest that A different part of the bill follows an earlier timetable. Schedule 1, including expanded powers for the eSafety Commissioner over apps and websites used to generate fake nude material, is due to take effect the day after Royal Assent.

Expanded eSafety powers start sooner than the digital duty and the court remedy.

The court remedy follows the 12-month timetable.

Calendar dates depend on when Royal Assent occurs. Branches show the sequence only.

Industry observers note that maps commencement rules for schedules 1 and 2 and the dated passage by Parliament. Connector lengths show sequence and branching.

In a recent development, calendar dates depend on when Royal Assent occurs. Branches show the sequence only.

Section 28D covers providers of services that use an internet carriage service to generate material with AI. That brings covered AI chatbots within the scope of the private court remedy. The provision also names social media services, relevant electronic services and designated internet services.

Industry observers note that A claimant would need to show that the provider failed to comply with its safety duty and that the failure caused their loss or damage. The bill treats that connection as established if the breach substantially contributed to the loss or damage.

Recent findings suggest that the duty requires providers to take appropriate safety measures, including effective steps to address the risks they identify in their assessments. The explanatory memorandum, quoted by the Senate committee, states a harmful interaction does not necessarily establish a breach. The provider’s response to reasonably foreseeable risks matters, including whether it put effective safeguards in place and kept them working.

If a claim succeeds, the court could award damages, including for emotional distress, issue an injunction or order the provider to apologize. The bill gives courts discretion to choose a remedy suited to the circumstances.

It has been revealed that the time limit for bringing a claim is tied to the claimant’s age and the date they suffered the loss or damage. Under section 28E, proceedings must begin before the later of their 21st birthday or six years after the day they suffered the loss or damage.

It has been revealed that for someone who is already 21 when they suffer the loss, the six-year period gives the later date. For someone who suffers loss or damage as a child, the 21st birthday can be the later date, depending on their age when they suffered the loss.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has opened its first Semi Megacharger in Texas, an 8-stall station in Mesquite on the east side of Dallas. With it, Tesla’s map now lists 7 public Megacharger sites and 44 stalls for its electric truck.

Industry observers note that that’s progress. But with six weeks left in 2026, it’s less than a fifth of the 37 sites Tesla planned to have open this year.

Tesla Charging announced the upcoming station on X on Tuesday night with its usual one-liner and a photo of the stalls at sunset:.

Newly introduced Tesla Megacharger: Mesquite, TX (8 stalls) https://t.co/UsCFMyCjo7 pic.twitter.com/W4G1e2BHkb.

Tesla’s map lists the site at 2175 S Town East Blvd in Mesquite, with eight Megachargers rated at up to 1.2 MW each.

Texas is where Tesla has the most riding on this network. When Tesla added 64 Megacharger locations to its map in February, Texas got 19 of the 66 planned sites, more than any other state. Mesquite is the first of them to go live, and several other Dallas–Fort Worth sites are still marked “coming soon.”.

The Pilot truck stop rollout hasn’t reached Texas either. When Pilot opened its first Megacharger in Georgia in October, it named a Flying J in Fort Stockton, Texas, as one of the next sites. It’s still not live on Tesla’s map.

Tesla also isn’t alone in DFW. Greenlane, the truck charging joint venture between Daimler Truck, NextEra and BlackRock, declared high-power sites in Dallas and Houston in May, open to any electric truck with CCS and MCS connectors. Tesla now has a station operating in the metro.

Here’s every public Megacharger at the moment live on Tesla’s map:.

That’s 7 sites and 44 stalls in four states. When we counted in early October, there were four customer-facing sites with 26 stalls. Tulare opened the same week, Hodgkins came on November 10, and now Mesquite.

So Tesla is adding a site roughly every two weeks.

It has been revealed that tesla also runs private Megachargers for its own fleet at Giga Nevada and in Carson, California, and it sells Megachargers to fleets and depot operators through its business program. Forum Mobility switched on two at the Port of Long Beach earlier this month. None of those count toward the public network that Semi buyers without their own depot rely on.

Tesla’s Q4 2025 shareholder report showed about 37 Megacharger sites for 2026. Semi program lead Dan Priestley has said Tesla wants 46 by early 2027.

To me this seems like good progress, sure it's not right on time with their ambitious goal, but they are executing on their charging network and I'm sure more sites will keep opening.

To hit 37, Tesla would need to open 30 more sites in the next 43 days. At the current pace, it ends the year with around 10.

It has been revealed that pilot noted in October that nine more of its sites were under construction, so a late burst is possible. But it would have to be a very major one.

Industry observers note that and the trucks are starting to show up. Tesla launched volume production of the Semi in September at a Nevada factory it says can build 50,000 trucks a year, and it remarked last week that Chicago’s first 50 Semis are en route for delivery, a day after Hodgkins opened. Massive fleets like that customer are installing their own depot chargers anyway, and most Semi charging will happen there. The public network is what lets a Semi leave its home region.

  • Bitcoin whales have defied the negative trend seen in the Q4s of the past nine years as they have accumulated billions of dollars' worth of Bitcoin since Q4 2026 began.
  • Even though Bitcoin has faced severe price corrections during the period, with its price retesting levels not seen this year, Bitcoin whales have continued to buy the asset.
  • Onchain data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant demonstrates that Bitcoin wallet addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC have increased their holdings by 121,117 BTC in Q4 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin whales have defied the negative trend seen in the Q4s of the past nine years as they have accumulated billions of dollars' worth of Bitcoin since Q4 2026 began.

Even though Bitcoin has faced severe price corrections during the period, with its price retesting levels not seen this year, Bitcoin whales have continued to buy the asset.

Onchain data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant demonstrates that Bitcoin wallet addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC have increased their holdings by 121,117 BTC in Q4 2026.

This defies the trend seen in the last nine Q4s, as Bitcoin whales have historically reduced their holdings during Q4 of each of the last nine years.

The source shared historic data from 2017, revealing that the Bitcoin whales recorded balance declines in seven of the last nine Q4 periods, with only 2019 and 2020 recording increases.

This means that the increase seen this month marks a major reversal of that historical trend, especially as Bitcoin has suffered even bigger price losses this Q4, dropping by about 29.5% over the same 52-day period.

Following the increase in Bitcoin whale accumulation seen in this quarter, further data shows that the whales now hold about 2.947 million BTC as of November 21, 2026.

Despite the increase in the holdings of Bitcoin whales this Q4, data also revealed that these large holders have seen their unrealized profits drop significantly.

As such, unrealized profits among addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have fallen to about $23.8 billion. Notably, this represents a massive decrease from the $124.7 billion recorded on September 30 and the record $294.4 billion in gains achieved on August 14, 2025.

This suggested that traders have been becoming more defensive and adding protection against a potential Bitcoin price decline.

Generally then, with the growing put/call ratio and elevated short interest, it would seem that traders may be bracing for further downside. They might not be anticipating a swift rebound either.

According to recent reports, in short, Bitcoin is showing early signs of a potential bottom. However, shrinking stablecoin liquidity, record ETF outflows, and rising demand for downside protection allude to the presence of bearish pressure. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • 27, Bitcoin developer Peter Todd warned that Google's blueprint to publicly display developers' addresses on the Play Store could lead to home invasions targeting developers of Bitcoin apps.
  • For independent developers working from home, the address displayed on Google Play could also be their residential address.
  • "There will be home invasions to compromise developers," Todd wrote on X.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 27, Bitcoin developer Peter Todd warned that Google's blueprint to publicly display developers' addresses on the Play Store could lead to home invasions targeting developers of Bitcoin apps.

For independent developers working from home, the address displayed on Google Play could also be their residential address.

"There will be home invasions to compromise developers," Todd wrote on X.

He specifically highlighted the risks to developers of Bitcoin and other security-related apps, urging Google employees responsible for implementing the change to refuse to do so.

Starting March 1, 2027, Google Play will display the phone number and address of developers who use individual accounts to publish apps and identify themselves as traders.

Google explained that the requirement is related to its obligations as an online marketplace in the European Economic Area (EEA) and the UK.

The address and contact information will be visible to Play Store owners worldwide.

The question is what address a developer might have to disclose, even for a relatively small app.

Dodemaide explained that Google support had informed him that he couldn't use a post office box because the address had to match his verified residential address.

He said he was considering removing his app from 31 countries to protect his home address.

Dodemaide also asked whether Google would allow individual developers to use a verified business mailing address instead.

Google lists several types of developers who may need to consider whether they qualify as traders, including those who sell apps, offer in-app purchases or earn advertising revenue.

For example, someone publishing an app purely as a hobby could declare themselves a non-trader.

Developers who don't distribute their apps in the EEA or UK are also considered non-traders under the policy.

Recent findings suggest that existing account holders have until Feb. 1, 2027, to submit their trader declarations, one month before the contact information becomes publicly visible.

Developers creating latest accounts will need to make their declarations during account registration.

Google warns that failing to comply could prevent developers from updating their apps or result in their apps being removed from the Play Store globally.

Industry News: Vitamin C May Lower Your Risk of Cancer from Certain Processed Foods

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1043 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that while diving into a plate of bacon or noshing on some salami is always tasty, there’s been growing concern that compounds found in cured meats may raise the risk of cancer.
  • Recent findings suggest that now, new research published in the Journal of Theoretical Biology suggests a possible solution: Take a carefully timed vitamin C supplement.
  • Recent findings suggest that researchers stress that this doesn’t mean you should pop a vitamin C every time you have bacon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that while diving into a plate of bacon or noshing on some salami is always tasty, there’s been growing concern that compounds found in cured meats may raise the risk of cancer. Specifically, once they hit your stomach, nitrates and nitrites found in these foods can spark a chain reaction called nitrosation that allows carcinogens to develop. This isn’t just a meat-eating concern either: fruits and vegetables that have grown in areas affected by pollution can also lead to this chain reaction.

Recent findings suggest that now, new research published in the Journal of Theoretical Biology suggests a possible solution: Take a carefully timed vitamin C supplement. It can cut this chain reaction and, in theory, lower the odds that carcinogens will develop after eating certain foods linked to this reaction, according to the findings.

Recent findings suggest that researchers stress that this doesn’t mean you should pop a vitamin C every time you have bacon. But the findings raise a lot of questions about why this may work and how to actually put it into practice in a safe way. Here’s what the researcher behind the study and dietitians want you to keep in mind.

Sources indicate that meet the experts: Gordon R. McNicol, PhD, lead study author and postdoctoral scholar in the Department of Applied Mathematics at the University of Waterloo; Jessica Cording, MS, RD, registered dietitian and author of The Little Book of Game-Changers; and Keri Gans, MS, RD, registered dietitian and author of The Small Change Diet.

For the study, researchers developed a mathematical model that simulates how nitrates and nitrites travel through the body, and where they undergo chemical changes. The model looked at a range of areas, including the salivary glands, stomach, small intestine, and plasma (i.e. the liquid part of your blood). Researchers discovered that having vitamin C alongside foods that contain nitrates and nitrites may halt chain reactions that happen in the body, including nitrosation, which makes substances that are linked to cancer development.

The researchers also looked at whether taking vitamin C after each meal could help, and found that it may reduce the formation of nitrosation products linked with cancer risk. The boost was most meaningful when people had foods that contained nitrates and nitrites, like salami, bacon, and other processed meats.

The researchers also theorized that this may explain why certain types of produce that happen to contain both vitamin C and nitrates (like spinach) don’t seem to increase cancer risk, while others do.

It’s important to stress this: The study was based on a mathematical model and was not a clinical trial or data analysis. Because of that, it's hard to draw too many conclusions right now.

Industry observers note that still, this link isn’t out of nowhere. “Under acidic conditions in the stomach, nitrites can undergo chemical reactions that lead to the formation of potentially harmful N-nitroso compounds,” says Gordon R. McNicol, PhD, lead study author and postdoctoral scholar in the Department of Applied Mathematics at the University of Waterloo. “Vitamin C can interfere with these reactions, reducing the formation of these compounds.”.

It has been revealed that why vitamin C? “Vitamin C is an antioxidant,” points out Jessica Cording, MS, RD, registered dietitian and author of The Little Book of Game-Changers. Meaning, it helps to neutralize unstable molecules in the body—and may do the same for nitrosation.

Sources indicate that but the effectiveness of vitamin C depends on when it’s in the stomach compared to when these reactions happen, McNicol adds. “Our simulations suggest that taking vitamin C shortly after meals could be particularly effective, as this allows vitamin C to overlap more closely with periods when nitrosation would otherwise be relatively high,” he states.

Sources indicate that experts stress that it’s important to keep the study in perspective. “While the findings are promising, more research is needed to determine whether taking vitamin C after meals actually reduces cancer risk,” indicates Keri Gans, MS, RD, registered dietitian and author of The Small Change Diet.

Cording agrees, stressing that while the findings are “promising,” they’re still just based on a mathematical model at this point. “That said, getting enough vitamin C and other antioxidants, alongside nutrients like fiber and other beneficial plant compounds, has been associated with reduced risk of disease and with overall immune system function,” Cording claims. “There are lots of great reasons to include vitamin-C rich fruits and vegetables throughout the day.”.

In a recent development, there are other things to consider, like practicality and safety. “Our research does not establish that taking vitamin C supplements after every meal is necessary or advisable,” McNicol notes. “Although our simulations suggest that dividing a fixed daily supplement across meals may be more effective than taking the same amount at once, further experimental and clinical studies are needed to determine whether these strategies are effective and safe in people.”.

High doses of vitamin C from supplements can also lead to GI discomfort, including nausea and diarrhea, Gans points out.

For now, this is more of an interesting finding vs. an actual dietary recommendation. “Until we have more research, there's no reason to recommend intentionally adding extra vitamin C, whether from food or supplements, after every meal specifically to reduce cancer risk,” Gans states.

It has been revealed that carina Hsieh, MPH, is the deputy features editor of Women’s Health. She has more than a decade’s worth of experience working in media and has covered everything from beauty, fashion, travel, lifestyle, pets, to health.

She began her career as an intern in the fashion closet at Cosmopolitan where she worked her way up to Senior Sex & Relationships Editor. While covering women’s health there, she discovered her passion for health service journalism and took a break to get her Masters in Public Health. Post-grad school, she worked as a freelance writer and as The Daily Beast’s first Beauty, Health, and Wellness Reporter.

Industry observers note that carina is an alum of the Fashion Institute of Technology and the Yale School of Public Health. She and her French Bulldog, Bao Bao, split their time between Brooklyn and Connecticut. She enjoys reformer Pilates, (slow) running, and smelling the fancy toiletries in boutique fitness class locker rooms.

Amflow launches its first city e-bikes, packing huge torque and serious smart tech

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its high-performance Avinox-powered machines, but now the firm is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment.
  • And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its high-performance Avinox-powered machines, but now the firm is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment. The newly unveiled Amflow UE Carbon series marks the brand’s first move into the commuter e-bike market, combining a lightweight carbon fiber frame, powerful mid-drive motor, and a surprisingly long list of smart features designed for everyday riding.

And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.

The new Amflow UE series comes in two versions, the UE Carbon and the higher-end UE Carbon Pro, both built around a full-carbon fiber frame weighing just 2.35 kg (5.2 lb).

The complete bike weighs as little as 20.9 kg (46 lb), which is fairly impressive considering the amount of hardware Amflow has packed into it, including front suspension, a suspension dropper seatpost, integrated lighting, and cargo racks.

It has been revealed that both models use the Avinox M2 mid-drive motor, which delivers up to 125 Nm of torque. That’s an enormous amount of torque for a city bike, and should make short work of steep hills, especially when carrying groceries or other cargo. And to put things into perspective, a lot of city e-bikes have barely 60 Nm for torque, so Amflow is knocking it out of the park for urban power.

A removable 600 Wh battery provides a claimed maximum range of 132 km (82 miles) in the lowest power assist mode, while fast charging can refill the battery in just 2 hours and 23 minutes.

The bikes also feature Avinox’s intelligent traction control system and a fresh Auto Boost function that automatically provides additional assistance when the system detects demanding conditions, such as accelerating from a stop or climbing a steep hill.

In other words, riders get much of the sophisticated motor technology developed for high-performance electric mountain bikes, but in a package designed for commuting to work or picking up groceries.

The bike is listed as weighing 20.9 kg (46 lb), though that figure conveniently excludes the front and rear racks, mudguards, pedals, kickstand, bike lock, bottle cage, and chainguard. So figure a few extra pounds for all of that gear, and you’re in the right ballpark.

The main difference between the two models is their drivetrain.

The higher-end UE Carbon Pro ($3,899) uses a customized three-speed electronically shifted internally geared hub paired with a Gates carbon belt drive. That should make it particularly appealing to commuters who want a quiet, clean, low-maintenance setup without worrying about chain lubrication or derailleur adjustments.

The more affordable UE Carbon ($3,499) instead uses a 10-speed electronic derailleur developed with TRP.

Both models support automatic shifting, allowing the bike to handle gear changes without requiring the rider to constantly think about them.

Amflow has also gone fairly wild with the technology integration.

There’s a 1.4-inch touchscreen display mounted on the handlebars, a wireless phone charging mount offering 15W wireless charging or 20W USB-C charging, and integrated lighting with automatic low-light activation and brake-sensing functionality.

The bikes even include a hardened steel frame lock on the rear wheel, Apple Find My integration, and a Lost Mode feature that can lock down certain components if the bike is stolen.

Apple Watch connectivity allows riders to check their bike’s status and unlock it, while heart-rate-based assistance can automatically adjust motor output to help riders maintain a target heart rate zone.

Some of these features, like the security and tracking, are immediately effective for nearly all riders, while other high-tech features like the heart rate-based pedal assist can provide even more functionality for niche riders looking to bridge the gap between riding for transportation and riding for fitness.

Of course, all the fancy technology in the world doesn’t mean much if a commuter bike can’t handle everyday errands.

Fortunately, Amflow appears to have taken the practical side seriously.

The bikes feature a low step-through frame, upright riding position, 65 mm suspension fork, and a suspension dropper seatpost offering 125 mm of height adjustment and approximately 30 mm of suspension travel.

The 26×2.0-inch Maxxis tires should also provide a comfortable ride over less-than-perfect city streets.

There’s a front rack rated for 20 kg (44 lb) and a rear rack rated for 27 kg (59.5 lb), with the latter supporting the MIK HD mounting system for compatible accessories, including child seats.

The standard frame is designed to accommodate riders from 155 to 190 cm (5’1” to 6’3”), while a smaller version for riders down to 140 cm (4’7”) is expected in 2027.

I’ve been impressed with the technology coming out of the Avinox ecosystem, and it’s exciting to see that technology finally make its way into a more practical city-focused electric bicycle.

According to recent reports, as much as I love high-performance electric mountain bikes, the reality is that most people aren’t spending their mornings bombing down mountain trails. They’re commuting to work, dropping kids off at school, and running errands.

And that’s where electric bicycles can make an even bigger difference.

The Amflow UE series seems to take a refreshingly comprehensive approach to urban riding. The powerful motor is nice, but I’m arguably more interested in the belt drive, integrated security, cargo capacity, automatic shifting, and built-in phone charging.

In a recent development, those are the kinds of features that can make an electric bicycle genuinely easier to live with every day. And as someone who actually commutes with an e-bike each day as my main form of transportation, these bikes are really speaking to me!

According to recent reports, if you ask me, it’s great to see another high-performance e-bike manufacturer recognizing that the future of electric bicycles isn’t just about riding farther and faster on trails. It’s also about making everyday transportation better for the less exciting type of riding, too.

  • Sources indicate that the Statistics Bureau of Japan remarked preliminary consumer prices across Tokyo's 23 wards rose 2.9% from a year earlier excluding fresh food, up from 2.6% in October.
  • In a recent development, electricity and city gas explain much of the split.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The yen slipped against the dollar on Friday, cutting the dollar cost of repaying fixed, unhedged yen loans for traders who borrowed the currency to buy Bitcoin. Bitcoin held above 60,000 USDT on Binance during Tokyo trading as two measures of the city's November inflation moved in opposite directions. Monday's two-year government bond auction is the next chance to see whether the yen and short-term yields move higher together.

Sources indicate that the Statistics Bureau of Japan remarked preliminary consumer prices across Tokyo's 23 wards rose 2.9% from a year earlier excluding fresh food, up from 2.6% in October. When energy is also excluded, inflation slowed to 2.5% from 2.6%. The preliminary Tokyo figures offer an early read ahead of the national release.

In a recent development, electricity and city gas explain much of the split. Electricity prices rose 9.5% from a year earlier, up from 1.7% in October, and city gas prices rose 13.7%, up from 4.9%. Energy's contribution to the headline inflation rate increased by 0.34 percentage points. The overall rate rose more modestly, to 2.8% from 2.7%, as other categories offset part of that increase. The bureau put the increase in electricity's contribution at 0.22 percentage points, and city gas at 0.11.

Both Tokyo gauges were at 2.6% in October. In November the measure that includes energy rose, while the measure that excludes it slowed.

Electricity and city gas accounted for most of the increase in energy’s contribution to Tokyo’s headline inflation rate.

November values are preliminary and cover Tokyo’s 23 wards. Electricity and city gas are included in the energy total, and the printed contributions are rounded.

The slopes share one vertical scale and use reported year-over-year Tokyo CPI rates. The zero-based bars show the bureau’s reported October-to-November changes in contributions to the all-items rate.

Industry observers note that november values are preliminary and cover Tokyo’s 23 wards. Electricity and city gas are included in the energy total, and the printed contributions are rounded.

Sources indicate that the dollar bought 159.28 to 159.30 yen at 9 a.m. Friday and 159.33 to 159.35 yen at 5 p.m., according to the Bank of Japan's Friday quotes. That compared with 159.16 to 159.18 yen at 5 p.m. Thursday. Both quotes use Tokyo time.

CoinGlass’s daily Binance data highlighted Bitcoin trading as low as 60,472 USDT on Nov. 27 as of 11:54 a.m. UTC. CryptoSlate's Bitcoin price tracker put it at $61,529 as of 11:57 a.m. UTC on Friday.

Sources indicate that ahead of the release, the risk for yen-funded Bitcoin trades was that hotter inflation could push the currency and short-term yields higher. An investor who borrows yen to buy Bitcoin and leaves the currency risk unhedged has to buy yen back to repay the loan. When the yen strengthens, the investor needs more dollars to repay the same yen balance even if Bitcoin's dollar price stands still. Friday's weaker yen moved that cost in the other direction.

In a recent development, interest costs move on a different timetable. A trader pays more in interest if a yen loan has to be replaced at a higher rate. The actual rate and the timing depend on the instrument, maturity and any hedge, so traders with similar Bitcoin positions can face different costs.

It has been revealed that japan's Ministry of Finance has scheduled the November 30 two-year bond auction notice for 10:30 a.m. Tokyo time and the public result for 12:35 p.m. At October’s two-year auction, the yield at the weighted-average accepted price was 1.91%, giving traders a benchmark for the fresh issue.

The auction yield measures the return implied by the price paid for the fresh bonds. The two-year yield in secondary trading just before and after the result can show whether investors are repricing the path of Japanese rates. If that market yield rises while the yen strengthens against the dollar, borrowers who need to refinance could face dearer loans just as their outstanding yen debt becomes more expensive in dollars. If yields rise and the yen stays weak, the signals would still be split.

Even a move in both markets would leave open how many Bitcoin positions use yen funding. Bank for International Settlements researchers documented how hard it was to size the broader currency carry trade after the August 2024 unwind.

Ethereum developers have agreed to move ahead with the next step in the Glamsterdam upgrade.

The key takeaway? Reaching consensus was not easy. Developers flagged potential network disruptions and usability issues with the fresh gas opcode. Still, they decided to proceed with it. In fact, the team also agreed to schedule the Hoodi testnet upgrade for 15th December at 7:12 PM UTC, moving Glamsterdam testing closer to implementation. So, what does this tell us?

It has been revealed that as highlighted in the developer’ discussion, Ethereum is emphasizing post-quantum security within its development, in addition to focusing on on-chain enhancements. Simply put, regardless of the ongoing concerns, the developers are clearly moving away from just looking at scaling and speed, and towards ensuring Ethereum is future-proof in relation to quantum computing.

It has been revealed that the meeting focused on deciding the scope and timing of the Glamsterdam upgrade and the prioritization of post-quantum security features. The execution layer teams reached a rough consensus to proceed with the current Glamsterdam spec as is, with the Hoodi testnet upgrade scheduled for December 15 at 7:12 PM UTC.

Interestingly, this was also reflected in the debate around the upcoming Heze upgrade.

According to recent reports, there was debate about whether to support Fossil or to place a bigger emphasis on post-quantum work. Concern was expressed that Fossil may also require development effort. Though no conclusion was reached, the matter will be discussed further at the next team meeting. Meanwhile, Kevaundray suggested that Keccak256 should be used as the hashing algorithm for Ethereum’s post-quantum work.

Against this backdrop, the Heze upgrade moving forward does not seem far-fetched. With the Hoodi upgrade scheduled and Keccak256 proposed for post-quantum security, Ethereum’s [ETH] focus on strengthening its long-term security is now becoming clearer.

The Hoodi testnet is a testing version of Ethereum that allows developers to trial upcoming upgrades.

According to recent reports, think of it as a testing ground where developers can identify bugs and ensure upgrades like Glamsterdam work smoothly before reaching Ethereum people. Within the wider scope of Ethereum’s post-quantum development, it may also be used to test upcoming security features, again allowing developers to analyze how prepared they are to then apply these to the mainnet.

That makes Hoodi an notable test for Glamsterdam, giving developers a clearer picture of whether the upgrade is ready for mainnet. Why does this matter? Well, Glamsterdam aims to improve transaction processing. If successful, these changes could strengthen Ethereum’s network fundamentals. Here, the timing matters too.

In a recent development, as the chart reveals, Ethereum has processed just over 100 million transactions in Q4 so far. By comparison, the network averaged more than 200 million transactions per quarter in 2026. This puts Q4 activity well below its recent pace, with ETH’s technical structure also showing signs of weakness.

Against this backdrop, the Hoodi testnet upgrade could mark an important inflection point for Ethereum.

A successful rollout would bring Glamsterdam closer to mainnet deployment. In turn, the upgrade could boost Ethereum’s throughput, improve execution efficiency, and support stronger on-chain activity.

Ethereum developers are moving ahead with Glamsterdam while focusing more on future quantum security.

The XRP Ledger's native lending protocol entered a 14-day activation countdown on Friday after its amendments gained 29 of 35 validator votes, according to XRPScan. If support holds, the ledger will get native lending and borrowing as early as Dec. 11, for the first time since its launch in 2012.

Recent findings suggest that hussein Zangana, director of community at the XRP Ledger Foundation, cast the 29th vote with his validator and revealed it in an X post on Friday. "I vote now for the Lending Protocol on the XRP Ledger and it's now in activation with 29 Yes votes," Zangana wrote.

𝗜 𝘃𝗼𝘁𝗲 𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 Lending Protocol 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 XRP Ledger and it's now in activation with 29 Yes votes. 𝗩𝗲𝘁 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗲𝘀📝: Lending and borrowing unlock capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger, provide yield and make XRP and XRPL assets usable as collateral. I appreciate the efforts exercised by the community to give this amendment a good screening! For validators this is important assistance and help in making educated decisions. Let's dive into why i voted Yes for Lending on XRP🧵.

According to XRPScan, LendingProtocol and its update LendingProtocolV1_1 both reached 29 votes on Friday. The earliest activation date for LendingProtocolV1_1 is Dec. 11, and its support has to stay above 80% until then. SingleAssetVault, the third amendment in the package, has 30 votes and can activate as early as Dec. 9.

"Lending and borrowing unlock capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger, provide yield and make XRP and XRPL assets usable as collateral," Zangana added in the same post.

Ripple engineer Vito Tumas first proposed the protocol in April 2024. According to the XLS-65 standard, each Single Asset Vault holds only one asset, such as XRP or RLUSD, and depositors get vault shares in the form of Multi-Purpose Tokens.

Under XLS-66, a loan broker uses that capital to glitch loans with a fixed term and a fixed rate. The broker checks borrowers off-chain and can post its own first-loss capital to cover defaults. Interest payments go back into the vault, and the protocol has no on-chain liquidations.

According to recent reports, "Represent value. Move value. Trade value. Now: finance value," Jazzi Cooper, head of product at RippleX, wrote on X about the vote. According to Cooper, the team made "deliberate design decisions: protocol native, built-in compliance, and off-chain underwriting.".

J. Ayo Akinyele, head of engineering at RippleX, wrote that the vaults and the protocol went through "multiple independent audits, a public Attackathon, formal verification, AI-assisted reviews, community testing, and validator review." Ripple and Common Prefix did the formal verification in the Lean 4 theorem prover. "Traditional testing isn't enough when you're building DeFi directly into Layer-1," Tumas wrote.

Clearpool said that it would bring "real-world, institutional-ready lending infrastructure, built natively on XRPL." The platform prepares a credit fund on the ledger with Ripple and Cicada Partners, and it has already tested a full loan cycle on Devnet. "We want to make real loans to real businesses," Tom Lombardi of Cicada Partners said.

Evernorth CEO Ashish Birla stated that his organization "is exploring how XLS-66 could support yield generation as part of our broader treasury strategy.".

In a recent development, according to XRPScan, SingleAssetVault can go live on Dec. 9, and the two lending amendments can follow on Dec. 11 if their support holds.

In a recent development, "Give it up, Bitcoiners. There is no such thing as money that is not used in exchange," Tucker wrote on X.

Recent findings suggest that tucker argued that Bitcoiners had brought the criticism upon themselves. They made the mistake of thinking they could simply declare Bitcoin a store of value and that would somehow make it one. That is not how it works, according to Tucker. He argued that nothing in the history of money supports this idea.

In his response, Saylor started with an example involving a bakery. Suppose someone buys bread at a bakery. They pay for the bread with a gold-backed banknote. The baker can use that banknote to pay the miller. The miller can use it to pay the farmer. All three transactions could be completed using the same banknote, while the gold stays in the vault.

In a recent development, @jeffreytucker Jeffrey, a gold-backed banknote could pay the baker, the miller, and the farmer while the gold stayed in the vault. Today people pay in dollars and save in gold, stocks, and real estate. Bitcoin is competing for those savings.

In the second part of his response, Saylor made an argument familiar to anyone who gets paid in dollars.

Industry observers note that sure, you can use dollars to buy groceries. However, you can still decide to keep some of your wealth in stocks, gold, or real estate.

It has been revealed that "Today people pay in dollars and save in gold, stocks, and real estate. Bitcoin is competing for those savings," Saylor wrote.

This last point was less ambitious than the claim Tucker was pushing back against.

Tucker was talking about Bitcoin becoming the world's most valuable asset.

Saylor, meanwhile, was making a simpler argument about where people choose to keep their savings.

However, Saylor's gold analogy raises an interesting question for Tucker. In Saylor's example, gold is still relevant to the purchase of bread because it backs the banknote the baker accepts.

However, in his modern examples, someone who chooses to save in stocks isn't necessarily concerned about whether their local bakery accepts stocks as payment.

For Tucker, it's all about how the customer pays for a loaf of bread. For Saylor, it's about what the baker does with the money after selling it.

  • The decision was revealed in the Co-chairs’ Statement following the ASEAN+3 Finance and Central Bank Deputies’ Meeting held in Kyoto, Japan recently.
  • Here, the initiative aims to strengthen regional financial cooperation by improving payment connectivity and encouraging discussions on how crypto should be regulated across participating economies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Given the rise in the acceptance of digital assets, the ASEAN+3 member countries have agreed to establish a dedicated working group to advance discussions on cross-border digital payments and regulatory approaches to digital assets.

The decision was revealed in the Co-chairs’ Statement following the ASEAN+3 Finance and Central Bank Deputies’ Meeting held in Kyoto, Japan recently.

Here, the initiative aims to strengthen regional financial cooperation by improving payment connectivity and encouraging discussions on how crypto should be regulated across participating economies.

In fact, it also marks a step towards greater coordination among Asian financial authorities as digital assets and blockchain-based financial services continue to expand.

To make this successful, the proposed working group aims to operate under the newly established AMRO Cross-Border Digital Payments Program. Under the same, they will provide a dedicated platform for ASEAN+3 economies to discuss retail and wholesale payment connectivity, alongside regulatory approaches to digital assets.

This is particularly important because cross-border payments remain fragmented across different financial systems. Needless to say, differences in payment infrastructure, regulations, and compliance requirements make international transactions slower and more expensive.

However, with greater coordination, participating economies could explore inter-operable payment systems and more consistent regulatory approaches.

Interestingly, the development also comes amid broader efforts by governments and financial regulators to address the growing influence of cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, and tokenized assets.

In a recent development, one prominent example is the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework. It became fully applicable on 30th December 2024, following the introduction of stablecoin-specific provisions in June 2024.

According to recent reports, for those unaware, MiCA establishes common rules for crypto-asset issuers and service providers, covering authorization, transparency, investor protection, and market conduct. Its implementation has provided a regulatory benchmark for other jurisdictions considering comprehensive crypto frameworks.

In a recent development, south Africa is another example of this shift. In August 2026, the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) and National Treasury proposed an activity-based reporting framework for cross-border crypto transactions.

Industry observers note that the proposal focuses on identifying and monitoring transactions that could facilitate capital flight, illegal financial flows, or regulatory circumvention. Rather than classifying crypto assets as official currency, it seeks to bring their cross-border movement under closer financial safeguards.

Sources indicate that on the other hand, the United States has faced setbacks in establishing similar regulatory clarity. The proposed Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate on 15th September, receiving 49 votes in favor and 50 against. it was short of the 60 votes required to proceed.

According to recent reports, its failure has left the U.S without the proposed comprehensive federal market structure framework, potentially putting it behind jurisdictions such as the E.U in providing regulatory certainty. However, the SEC and CFTC continue to pursue regulatory initiatives under their existing authority.

Against this backdrop, ASEAN+3’s latest decision is the latest in the world’s global regulatory discussion/efforts.

Recent findings suggest that the experience of being a team player has come in handy for Jade as she navigates the world of wrestling. Sure, it may often look like a one-on-one competition, but Jade says that, if anything, it’s more like a dance.

Industry observers note that “I can only be as great as my partner,” she tells editors Abigail Cuffey, Amanda Lucci, and Jacqueline Andriakos on the latest episode of The Huddle. “I can't do this by myself.”.

Industry observers note that despite having been a part of the WWE since 2023, Jade admits she’s still a “rookie” compared to her ‘dance’ partners—the other women in the league, who inspire her every day. “I've been placed in a very amazing environment with women who strive for greatness, and that's what I want to do,” she states.

As she prepares to lead a five-woman team at Survivor Series: WarGames on November 28, Jade talks about her unconventional path to wrestling, making peace with mistakes, and the advice she wants every kid watching her to hear.

Sources indicate that jade’s journey to becoming a professional wrestler is the stuff of motivational sports movies. A stay-at-home mom (she took time off work as a child psychologist to raise her daughter), Jade was simply training in the gym to get strong after pregnancy when she was introduced to WWE veteran Mark Henry, who asked if she’d ever considered a career in wrestling.

“I was like, ‘Why not?’” she recalls thinking. “I had a kid and put my life on hold for a little bit. I wanted to do something more. I was like, ‘This body is not done.’ [I] went to a tryout, had no experience at all.”.

According to recent reports, jade left that tryout bruised and battered—and determined to improve. And so she trained and trained and trained some more. She couldn’t get enough. “I just loved it,” she claims. “It's athletics, yes, but also it's improvising, but also it's acting, but also it's your natural instinct. It’s all these things wrapped into one that I just didn't want to put down.”.

All that work eventually paid off: Jade made her professional wrestling debut with All Elite Wrestling in 2020 and then joined the WWE three years later.

Despite all the training and preparation that goes into a match, Jade admits that not a single one has been “perfect.” But in the case where she stumbles off the ropes or throws a lousy punch, Jade simply follows the old maxim, the show must go on.

Sources indicate that “I just kind of have the mindset that these things happen,” she says. “If you do have a mishap, you can't sell it—[the audience doesn’t] know what's going on. You just got to keep going with the punches.”.

Jade also gives a lot of credit to her fellow competitors, who often pick her up—if not physically, then emotionally—after a match, letting her know she’s not alone.

In a recent development, “I remember my coworker Naomi sent me a clip of her falling, and she was like, ‘Just to show you...’ And I was like, ‘Okay, all right. It happens,’” Jade says. “You’ve just got to keep on going and make your next match the best match.”.

Industry observers note that as a mom, Jade knows how powerful an adult’s example can be—whether it’s a parent’s or a performer’s. Ultimately, she hopes kids are inspired by her hard work and determination, both in and out of the ring, and if they can take away any message, it would be this: “Don't let anyone tell you who you are,” she claims. “Don't let society put you in a box. Go out there and take on the world.”.

It has been revealed that and when a new opportunity presents itself, don’t be afraid to give it a try. “If you would have told me five years ago, I would be wrestling. I would have laughed,” she claims. “And look at me now.”.

#156157. Why So Many Upcoming Moms Are Told to Wait to Exercise Again—and What the Research Really States

Why So Many Upcoming Moms Are Told to Wait to Exercise Again—and What the Research Really States

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1894 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earlier this year, trainer and WH advisory board member Sohee Carpenter, CSCS, posted an Instagram Reel challenging some conventional postpartum advice: Don’t work out until your ob-gyn clears you at your six-week follow-up appointment.
  • Sources indicate that “I feel like so many people get angry because they assume we mean you're going to be doing a one-rep max back squat a week after you have a baby,” Carpenter says.
  • The problem, Carpenter explains, is that the six-week rule isn’t based on evidence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earlier this year, trainer and WH advisory board member Sohee Carpenter, CSCS, posted an Instagram Reel challenging some conventional postpartum advice: Don’t work out until your ob-gyn clears you at your six-week follow-up appointment. Her point wasn’t that new moms should rush back to the gym. It was that one timeline can’t fit everyone. Some women are ready to move sooner, and others need more time.

The Reel ruffled some feathers.

Sources indicate that “I feel like so many people get angry because they assume we mean you're going to be doing a one-rep max back squat a week after you have a baby,” Carpenter says. “But that's definitely not what we're saying.” (By “we,” she means trainers who keep up with the latest research on pregnancy and postpartum exercise.).

The problem, Carpenter explains, is that the six-week rule isn’t based on evidence. On the contrary, research suggests that this type of blanket advice doesn’t make sense for something as personal as postpartum recovery. When you return to exercise after childbirth should depend on your own symptoms, not a date on the calendar.

“There's really nothing magical about the six-week time point,” says Margie Davenport, PhD, a professor of kinesiology at the University of Alberta and chair of the 2025 Canadian Guidelines for Physical Activity for Pregnancy and Postpartum—the first-ever exercise guidelines to specifically focus on evidence-based suggestions for that first year postpartum. In the U.S., the main guidance from the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) covers pregnancy and the postpartum period together. ACOG’s guidance points in the same direction, though: It says many women can start exercising again within days of an uncomplicated birth. In fact, “there is no identified ideal time to return,” Davenport says.

In a recent development, based on the wide range of comments on Carpenter’s post—some supportive, some hypercritical, and still others asking more questions to try to better understand this shift away from the advice they’ve always heard—there’s still a lot of confusion around postpartum exercise. So we asked experts to break down what the research actually says, and how to approach working out in this latest chapter of life.

In many cultures, the first 30 or 40 days postpartum is traditionally considered a protected time to rest, relax, and recover, Davenport says. In Chinese culture, it’s called zuo yuezi, which translates to “sitting the month.” In many Latin American and Latino communities, it’s known as “la cuarentena,” a nod to its roughly 40-day length. In South Korea, it’s sanhujori, or “postpartum care.”.

According to recent reports, these traditions carry deep cultural significance and are meant to offer real healing and support after birth from one’s community (they put “it takes a village” into practice). They’re rooted in caregiving and cultural custom, and they were never meant to serve as a medical timeline for when it’s safe to start exercising.

Sources indicate that in Western medicine, six weeks has become an crucial medical benchmark in postpartum recovery—and, over time, a default point for returning to exercise too. “At that point, your uterus should be back to its pre-pregnancy state, and so a lot of the gynecologic changes should be fairly reversed by that point,” says Rita Deering, DPT, PhD, associate professor of exercise science and director of the Pelvic Health, Exercise & Musculoskeletal (PHEM) Research Laboratory at Marquette University.

Sources indicate that the first six weeks after birth are also when the risk of complications like high blood pressure and infection is highest, Deering says, which is part of why that window became an vital medical checkpoint (even though some pregnancy-related changes take longer to resolve). But, she says, “it was never intended to be about exercise.”.

So how did six weeks become the exercise rule? Before researchers knew much about how safe it is to exercise during pregnancy and after birth, working out was considered potentially risky, Deering says. There wasn’t strong evidence that exercise wouldn’t slow healing or raise the odds of complications. So the most cautious advice was simply to wait until a doctor confirmed you’d healed enough to resume physical activity.

To come up with the 2025 Canadian Guidelines, researchers did a deep dive of all the available research on the topic, which included 574 unique studies organized into seven systematic reviews based on 21 different outcomes of postpartum exercise—such as depression and anxiety, low-back pain, injuries, glucose and blood pressure levels, and more. They also assembled an international panel of experts to give their recommendations.

Their advice: Start light-intensity physical activity and mobilization (think: carrying your baby around your home, a slow walk down the block, pelvic floor physical therapy) right away. From there, progress as you feel ready to moderate-to-vigorous activity such as brisk walking, resistance training, and running at your own pace—as long as tears and incisions have sufficiently healed and you don’t experience additional bleeding with exercise. (As mentioned, ACOG similarly recommends that women can return to postnatal exercise within days after an uncomplicated birth.).

Based on the research, there are no “absolute contraindications” to exercise postpartum, Davenport notes—meaning no condition would rule out exercise entirely. There are some relative contraindications, she explains, “where you might have to delay a little bit or modify the type of activity that you're doing.” Examples include severe abdominal pain, extreme fatigue, and C-section incision pain that worsens with activity. All warrant a conversation with your doctor before starting.

Recent findings suggest that want to Know More About Lifting While Pregnant? Start Here.

Pelvic floor symptoms, like leaking urine or a feeling of heaviness in the vagina, aren’t a reason to stop exercising altogether. If you notice signs of pelvic floor dysfunction, the guidelines recommend starting slowly and building up gradually instead. “Some leakage is okay,” Davenport says. “It means that the training that you’re doing is just overloading the muscle.”.

Many people, including plenty of commenters on Carpenter’s Reel, worry that exercising after birth will damage the pelvic floor and cause dysfunction. But the evidence doesn’t support that. In fact, those muscles will likely be better off if you resume training, especially if you do exercises to target them in particular. “Engaging in pelvic floor muscle training reduces your risk of urinary incontinence by around 37 percent,” Davenport states. Additionally, if you stop all exercise because you're leaking a little bit, “this can actually mean that you're missing out on those other benefits.”.

Industry observers note that one caveat: If you’re leaking a lot, or it’s getting worse over time, “you probably need to pull it back,” Davenport states. That means being more selective about the moves you choose. For example, you might skip long runs and high-impact moves like jump squats for now, adds Sheridan Skye, a registered nurse, pre- and postnatal fitness coach, and founder of The Female Fitness Formula. Stick with lower-impact exercises, then build up gradually as you get stronger and your symptoms level off or improve.

At the end of the day, every body, birth, and recovery is vastly different. “Some people have a very uncomplicated labor and delivery and pregnancy; for others, it's quite complex,” says Davenport. “It only makes sense that the way that they're returning and what time they're actually returning is also going to be quite individualized.”.

According to recent reports, for some fresh moms, six weeks is too soon, and a blanket deadline only adds stress. “Maybe they aren't sleeping or they don't have the support to be able to return [to exercise] at six weeks,” Davenport states. On the flip side, for someone who had a straightforward delivery and is itching to get moving again, “telling them to wait for six weeks with no evidence to support it is also inappropriate.”.

In fact, exercise can offer significant benefits during postpartum recovery, even before the six-week mark. “It improves muscle and bone density that we lose throughout pregnancy,” Skye states. Postpartum exercise is associated with a 45 percent reduction in the odds of developing postpartum depression, and starting before 12 weeks is even more beneficial.

It’s also associated with a 28 percent reduction in the risk of developing diabetes postpartum. Exercise even improves sleep quality, Skye notes. “Women tend to feel more energized and like they've experienced more rest, even if they haven't,” she says. (Anyone who’s survived a 3 a.m. feeding stretch knows that’s no small thing!).

Recent findings suggest that there is also evidence that exercise in general can help to decrease pain, claims Deering, and research links sedentary behavior to lumbopelvic (the areas of the lower back and pelvis) pain. “So if you are having pain, movement might be what you need to help with that.”.

Sources indicate that for many people, it may be difficult to know if you’re truly ready. “Especially when you're postpartum, it can feel like you are super out of touch with your body sensations, especially if you're not sleeping well,” Carpenter says.

Industry observers note that if you're at the point where you're thinking about it, but are nervous or unsure or just overwhelmed by having another decision to make, Davenport recommends taking the Get Active Questionnaire for Postpartum—a tool that her team designed as part of the 2025 guideline. It can help you quickly understand if you’re ready to start from a medical perspective. That can help give you some reassurance.

There can also be “a lot of fear involved,” Carpenter claims, especially if you had a C-section or are healing from a vaginal tear. In that case, “you’re probably going to be a bit hesitant,” which is completely understandable. Starting slower and lighter than you think you need to is perfectly fine as you get reacquainted with your body. “The first several sessions are really about mentally trying to get that confidence back,” she says.

Sources indicate that as you go, pay attention to how your body responds. Leaking, for instance? That’s not a reason to stop exercising, but you may want to adjust your workout to reduce it. More bleeding, new pain, or a sense that something just doesn’t feel right are signs to stop, reassess, and possibly scale back. If they don’t improve, check in with your doctor. “It’s really about setting your ego aside and being willing to modify, even if it’s one rep to the next, based on how you’re feeling right at that time,” Carpenter says.

And if you feel physically ready but aren’t quite there mentally? “It’s okay to honor those feelings,” Deering claims, “and to recognize that it’s okay to give yourself some time.” Whether that’s two weeks, six weeks, or six months, the right moment to start moving is the one that works for you.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that coinkite, the wallet's manufacturer, published its postmortem on Nov.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A security flaw in Coldcard's Bitcoin hardware wallets went undetected for more than five years despite at least 15 independent security research and review efforts.

Recent findings suggest that coinkite, the wallet's manufacturer, published its postmortem on Nov. 24, detailing how a firmware defect introduced in March 2021 weakened the recovery phrases generated by its devices, enabling attackers to steal customers' Bitcoin without accessing their hardware wallets.

According to recent reports, an Aug. 14 analysis by Galaxy Research identified with high confidence 1,778.84 BTC, worth $112.7 million at the time, stolen from more than 8,600 addresses. Galaxy estimated that losses could reach 2,417 BTC, or $153 million, if additional suspected thefts were confirmed.

Coinkite mentioned it had matched approximately 300 loss-related support tickets to 236 customer accounts, representing about 0.2% of its estimated user base. However, the manufacturer acknowledged that the actual number of affected customers was likely higher.

The vulnerability originated from a firmware configuration error that caused Coldcard devices to generate recovery phrases using a weaker software-based random number generator instead of the intended hardware component.

The devices continued producing apparently valid recovery phrases, allowing the defect to escape routine security and functionality tests.

Coinkite's postmortem estimates that the defect substantially reduced the randomness protecting recovery phrases across five Coldcard models, including the Mk2, Mk3, Mk4, Mk5 and Q.

Attackers exploited that weakness to reconstruct private keys offline and transfer Bitcoin from affected wallets.

Industry observers note that between 2021 and 2026, Coldcard underwent at least 15 independent security research and review efforts, including two paid third-party product reviews. Its publicly available firmware repository also had 54 contributors.

One commissioned review in March 2022 specifically examined random-number generation and related security measures without discovering the defect.

More recently, independent security researcher Rob Hamilton used OpenAI's Cybersecurity Harness to examine Coldcard's firmware between May 1 and June 26.

The AI-assisted review generated 85 potential security findings, several of which prompted fixes, but failed to identify the seed-generation vulnerability.

A separate June 17 review by security researcher Nick Farrow also examined weak random-number generation and concluded that the relevant implementation was sound.

Recent findings suggest that coinkite attributed these failures to a gap in its verification process. Existing checks established that the hardware random-number generator was present in the firmware but failed to confirm whether the software actually used it to create recovery phrases.

The company identified the defect on July 30, following the first reported thefts, and released corrected firmware the following day.

Security firm Keylabs subsequently verified the fix across four firmware releases for Coldcard's Mk5 and Q wallets.

Coinkite has also introduced additional safeguards that combine user-provided randomness with multiple hardware sources when generating fresh recovery phrases.

However, these changes cannot strengthen recovery phrases created using the defective firmware, leaving previously affected wallets exposed even after their owners install the latest updates.

According to recent reports, keylabs traced the seed-generation fix to four signed releases. Owners keeping a wallet still need to know how its original recovery phrase was created.

Coinkite advises moving funds to a fresh wallet if the original seed was affected or its origin is unclear.

The audit covers the seed-generation fix on the four listed standard releases. Coinkite’s migration guide details the qualifying dice exception and secure external imports.

The upper path follows the scope in Keylabs’ October 15 report. The lower path follows Coinkite’s affected-seed migration guidance.

Industry observers note that the audit covers the seed-generation fix on the four listed standard releases. Coinkite’s migration guide details the qualifying dice exception and secure external imports.

It has been revealed that coinkite said wallets using securely generated external recovery phrases were unaffected. Owners who incorporated at least 50 fair, independent and private dice rolls during their original wallet setup also remained protected if they followed the prescribed procedure.

The firm advises other affected owners to generate latest recovery phrases using verified firmware and transfer their Bitcoin to the resulting wallets.

Meanwhile, law enforcement continues investigating the thefts, and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security has opened a separate case.

Coinkite has appealed to whoever controls the stolen Bitcoin to return the funds. Nearly four months after the exploit, however, the firm has yet to decide whether it will compensate affected customers.

West Coast Customs turns a Tesla Model 3 into a 1955 Chevy Bel Air
